reasons: Covered by contentModel.test, which checks the page structure, the citations and the PowerPoint output.
Some page IDs and labels are built from counts, so they can shift when the content changes.
The factbase line is cut off in the packet, so its exact wording cannot be confirmed here.

terms.meaning: one line of text on a slide together with the record of where it came from
the record that says which facts, or which method, support a line of text
the full list of facts gathered for one project, including those not used in the analysis
splitting a long list of claims into several pages

sections.name: File setup, Claim, note
sections.title: Claim types and imports
sections.what: Defines a claim as a line of text plus its citation, and a helper for method notes that are not project findings.
sections.why: Every line on a slide carries a citation so the reader can trace it.
sections.watch_out: Notes labelled as method are not evidence about projects, so do not read them as findings.

sections.name: supported, gap
sections.title: Supported and gap claim helpers
sections.what: Makes a claim labelled as evidence when supporting facts exist, otherwise labelled as a gap, and a gap claim that states what is missing.
sections.why: Keeps missing evidence visible instead of hiding it.
sections.watch_out: Gap claims are shown on the slide on purpose, so empty sections appear with a gap message.

sections.name: interpretation
sections.title: Interpretation claim helper
sections.what: Works like a supported claim but marks the text as analysis, with a warning that the sources support the inputs and not a verified conclusion.
sections.why: Separates the authors' interpretation from reported facts.
sections.watch_out: Any inferred statement must use this helper rather than the plain one, or it will look like a sourced fact.

sections.name: buildCompleteContent (part 1)
sections.title: Cover, summary and structure pages
sections.what: Starts the content builder. Defines a section helper that splits claims into pages of about 1800 characters and up to ten items, with citations. Then builds the cover, the executive summary and the study structure.
sections.why: Pages are built before storage so the viewer and the export match.
sections.watch_out: Continuation pages get a numbered suffix on their ID, so renaming a section changes the stored IDs.

sections.name: buildCompleteContent (part 2)
sections.title: Framework, pillar and driver pages
sections.what: Adds the framework overview, a page for each pillar, and a page for each sub-driver with its rationale and facts. Each driver also gets example groups by rating (good practice, cautionary and mixed, neutral or ongoing). Then adds the assessment rubric page.
sections.why: Grouping by rating keeps good practice separate from failure, so a whole project is not called a failure from one criterion.
sections.watch_out: A judgement attaches to a driver by its ID, or by its text if no ID exists, so renaming a driver can break that link.

sections.name: buildCompleteContent: for
sections.title: Cross-case tables and synthesis
sections.what: For each pillar, builds driver tables in groups of four, and an evidence matrix. Then builds the full assessment synthesis and a cross-case synthesis list. Missing judgements are shown as unassessed.
sections.why: Blank cells are shown as unassessed instead of being guessed.
sections.watch_out: Shared fact IDs alone do not link a judgement to a driver, so the code checks the explicit driver link first.

sections.name: buildCompleteContent: for
sections.title: Project summaries, factbases and reference notes
sections.what: For each contributing project, writes a summary page and a complete factbase page listing every fact, including those not admitted and their reasons. Then adds programme, learning, method, abbreviation and closing pages.
sections.why: Each project's full record follows its summary so readers can check the basis of the summary.
sections.watch_out: The factbase line is cut off in the packet, so its exact wording is unclear here.

sections.name: buildCompleteContent: for
sections.title: Source pages and claim source index
sections.what: Adds one source page for each stored fact with its ID, status, URL, anchor and reasons. Then gathers every citation and writes one claim source index page per citation group, and returns all pages.
sections.why: Gives a traceable page for each piece of evidence.
sections.watch_out: Index page IDs include the group count and page count, so they change whenever the content changes.

summary: Builds the complete list of content pages for a lessons-learnt run, where every line carries a citation and every page is split to fit.
purpose: Creates the stored content that both the on-screen viewer and the PowerPoint export use, so they show the same pages.
why: The comment says content is paginated before it is stored, so viewers and exports receive identical pages.
how: Defines how a claim carries its citation, then a helper that splits claims into pages of up to about 1800 characters and ten items. It builds the cover, the executive summary, the framework, each pillar and its drivers, the examples by rating, the cross-case tables, each project summary and its full factbase, programme and learning notes, method, abbreviations, source pages, and finally a claim source index.
inputs: The run result parts: facts, pillars, projects, assessments, patterns, methodology and scope, plus an optional coverage record.
outputs: A list of slide blocks, each with a title, bullets, citations and metadata that says what kind of page it is.
risks: Claims are shown as unassessed when no judgement exists, so a missing judgement looks like a gap rather than an error. Page IDs change when content changes, so any saved links to pages may break. Several sections are very long, which makes edits risky.
debug: If a page is missing, check its section call and whether its facts were admitted, since only admitted facts are used for claims. If a citation looks wrong, check the citation grouping at the end. If a table row is blank, check the unassessed fallback and the driver link.
